---
title: "DC vehicle taxes: a 5% value tax over $40k, and a length surcharge"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
options(scipen = 999, width = 110, pillar.sigfig = 6)

dmv_file  <- "dmv_data_cleaned.csv"  # cleaned DMV new-registration data
len_file  <- "vehicle_lengths.csv"   # lengths of nameplates longer than a Camry (built for this note)
stock     <- 279262                  # DC household vehicles, ACS 2020-24 (B25046)

# ---- Part 1: value tax settings -------------------------------------------
rate      <- 0.05                    # value tax rate
threshold <- 40000                   # value tax applies to value above this
spread    <- 0.30                    # log-sd of prices within a brand

# ---- Part 2: length surcharge settings (edit these, then re-knit) ----------
fee_at_esv <- 300          # annual fee ($) for a vehicle as long as a 2025 Escalade ESV
curve      <- 1            # 1 = fee rises linearly with length; 2 = quadratic
fee_cap    <- fee_at_esv   # top fee ($) in the "capped" results; or type a dollar amount
L_camry    <- 193.5        # fee starts above this length (in.): 2025 Toyota Camry
L_esv      <- 227.0        # fee reaches fee_at_esv at this length (in.): 2025 Escalade ESV
commercial_types <- c("Van", "Heavy-duty pickup")  # vehicle types exempted as "commercial"
ext_share  <- 1/3          # share of lumped SUVs that are the long version (ESV, Expedition MAX, ...)
```

# Part 1. A 5% tax on vehicle value over $40,000

## 1. Prices when new

Kelley Blue Book average transaction prices by brand, October 2026. Brands not in the KBB table get rough guesses.

```{r prices}
atp <- c(ACURA = 50320, AUDI = 64403, BMW = 73149, BUICK = 37400, CADILLAC = 90101,
         CHEVROLET = 51058, CHRYSLER = 49959, DODGE = 53475, FORD = 61565, GENESIS = 64316,
         GMC = 65607, HONDA = 38198, HYUNDAI = 38320, INFINITI = 69865, JEEP = 53592,
         KIA = 39260, `LAND ROVER` = 102826, LEXUS = 63899, LINCOLN = 78132, MAZDA = 37082,
         MERCEDESBENZ = 71086, MINI = 41075, MITSUBISHI = 33579, NISSAN = 37578,
         PORSCHE = 125270, RAM = 69850, SUBARU = 37429, TESLA = 54194, TOYOTA = 44168,
         VOLKSWAGEN = 40185, VOLVO = 61588)
guesses <- c(JAGUAR = 70000, `ALFA ROMEO` = 50000, MASERATI = 100000, POLESTAR = 60000,
             LUCID = 90000, RIVIAN = 85000, FIAT = 30000, SMART = 25000, ASTONMARTIN = 250000,
             FERRARI = 250000, BENTLEY = 250000, LAMBORGHINI = 250000, ROLLSROYCE = 250000,
             `ROLLS ROYCE` = 250000, MCLAREN = 250000, MERCURY = 30000, PONTIAC = 30000,
             SATURN = 30000, SAAB = 35000, OLDSMOBILE = 30000, HUMMER = 60000, SCION = 25000,
             ISUZU = 35000, PLYMOUTH = 25000)
price_new <- c(atp, guesses)

# Industry average new price by model year (approximate), used to scale older cars back.
# Anchors: KBB put the 2018 average near $36,000 and October 2026 at $51,109.
atp_year <- c(`2015` = 33500, `2016` = 34500, `2017` = 35500, `2018` = 36500, `2019` = 37800,
              `2020` = 40000, `2021` = 45000, `2022` = 48500, `2023` = 48500, `2024` = 48500,
              `2025` = 49800, `2026` = 51109)
```

## 2. Which cars are still registered in DC

The DMV file counts cars *first registered* in DC each year. Assuming a constant share stays registered each year, that share is 1 − (2025 registrations ÷ total cars).

```{r stock}
dmv <- read_csv(dmv_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(weight_class %in% c("Class I", "Class II", "Class III"),
         make_clean %in% names(price_new))

inflow_2025 <- sum(dmv$n[dmv$year == 2025])
retention   <- 1 - inflow_2025 / stock

dmv <- dmv |> mutate(still_here = n * retention^(2025 - year))

c(inflow_2025 = inflow_2025, retention = round(retention, 3),
  modeled_stock = round(sum(dmv$still_here)))
```

## 3. Value today

Depreciation follows Kelley Blue Book's average rates for years 1–5 (16%, 12%, 11%, 9%, 7%), then 7% a year after that.

```{r value}
dep_rates  <- c(0.16, 0.12, 0.11, 0.09, rep(0.07, 150))  # long enough for 1920s cars
dep_factor <- c(1, cumprod(1 - dep_rates))   # share of value left at age 0, 1, 2, ...

scale_to_year <- function(my) {
  ifelse(my < 2015, 33500 / 51109 * 0.97^(2015 - my),
         atp_year[as.character(pmin(pmax(my, 2015), 2026))] / 51109)
}

dmv <- dmv |>
  mutate(age   = pmax(2025 - model_year, 0),
         value = unname(price_new[make_clean]) * scale_to_year(model_year) * dep_factor[age + 1])
```

## 4. Tax per car

Prices vary within a brand (a "Toyota" can be a $25k Corolla or a $75k Sequoia), so each brand-year's value is treated as the average of a lognormal distribution. The expected tax is then 5% of the expected amount above $40k.

```{r tax}
expected_excess <- function(mu, k = threshold, s = spread) {
  d1 <- (log(mu / k) + s^2 / 2) / s
  mu * pnorm(d1) - k * pnorm(d1 - s)
}
share_over <- function(mu, k = threshold, s = spread) pnorm((log(mu / k) + s^2 / 2) / s - s)

dmv <- dmv |>
  mutate(tax     = rate * expected_excess(value),
         p_taxed = share_over(value))
```

## Results

```{r results}
total <- dmv |> summarise(cars          = sum(still_here),
                          cars_taxed    = sum(still_here * p_taxed),
                          revenue_M     = sum(still_here * tax) / 1e6,
                          avg_tax_taxed = sum(still_here * tax) / sum(still_here * p_taxed))
round(total, 1)

dmv |>
  mutate(age_group = cut(age, c(-1, 0, 2, 5, 9, Inf),
                         labels = c("New", "1-2", "3-5", "6-9", "10+"))) |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarise(cars       = round(sum(still_here)),
            cars_taxed = round(sum(still_here * p_taxed)),
            revenue_M  = round(sum(still_here * tax) / 1e6, 1))
```

## Sensitivity

```{r sensitivity}
run <- function(s = spread, scale_back = TRUE) {
  v <- unname(price_new[dmv$make_clean]) * dep_factor[dmv$age + 1] *
       (if (scale_back) scale_to_year(dmv$model_year) else 1)
  ex <- if (s == 0) pmax(v - threshold, 0) else expected_excess(v, s = s)
  round(sum(dmv$still_here * rate * ex) / 1e6, 1)
}

tibble(variant   = c("Brand averages only (no spread)", "Central (spread 0.3)",
                     "Wider spread (0.4)", "Today's prices for all model years"),
       revenue_M = c(run(s = 0), run(), run(s = 0.4), run(scale_back = FALSE)))
```

# Part 2. An annual length surcharge

The surcharge is $0 for a vehicle no longer than a 2025 Toyota Camry (`r L_camry` in.). Above that it rises `r if (curve == 1) "in a straight line" else paste0("with the extra length raised to the power ", curve)`, reaching $`r fee_at_esv` at the length of a 2025 Cadillac Escalade ESV (`r L_esv` in.) and continuing upward beyond it. The "capped" results stop it at $`r fee_cap`. All of these settings live in the `setup` chunk at the top.

## 1. The schedule

```{r schedule}
surcharge <- function(len, cap = Inf) {
  pmin(fee_at_esv * (pmax(len - L_camry, 0) / (L_esv - L_camry))^curve, cap)
}

tribble(~vehicle,                           ~length_in,
        "Toyota Camry (2025)",              193.5,
        "Toyota Highlander (2020+)",        194.9,
        "Ford Explorer (2020+)",            198.8,
        "Toyota Sienna (2021+)",            203.7,
        "Chevrolet Tahoe (2021+)",          210.7,
        "Toyota Tacoma Double Cab (2024+)", 213.0,
        "Chevrolet Suburban (2021+)",       225.7,
        "Cadillac Escalade ESV (2021+)",    227.0,
        "Ford F-150 SuperCrew, 5.5 ft box", 231.7,
        "Ram ProMaster, 159 in. wheelbase", 236.2,
        "Ford Transit, extended length",    263.9) |>
  mutate(uncapped = round(surcharge(length_in)),
         capped   = round(surcharge(length_in, cap = fee_cap)))
```

## 2. Vehicle lengths

The DMV file has make, model and model year, but not trim, cab or wheelbase. `vehicle_lengths.csv` gives an overall length, one row per generation, for every nameplate longer than a Camry among those with five or more 2025 registrations (97% of vehicles), plus rarer big trucks, vans and SUVs. Anything not listed is treated as Camry-length or shorter. Two simplifications:

* **Pickups and vans** get their most common body (crew cab with short bed; 148-in. Transit; 159-in. ProMaster). Their shortest and longest bodies feed the sensitivity check.
* **Extended-length SUVs.** The DMV lumps some SUVs with their extended versions: Escalade ESV, Expedition MAX, Navigator L, Wagoneer L, Grand Cherokee L and the long-wheelbase Range Rover. `ext_share` sets how many are the long version.

Each `pattern` is a regular expression for the DMV `make_model` field. It also catches the six-letter truncations found in older records ("CHEVROLET SUBURB").

```{r lengths}
lengths <- read_csv(len_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

lk <- lengths |>
  mutate(make_model = map(pattern, \(p) str_subset(unique(dmv$make_model), p))) |>
  unnest(make_model)

# Every pattern matches something, and no nameplate matches two different patterns
stopifnot(all(lengths$pattern %in% lk$pattern),
          !anyDuplicated(distinct(lk, pattern, make_model)$make_model))

new25 <- dmv |> filter(year == 2025)

# One row per DMV record x length row; `share` splits records between body lengths.
# Vehicles in `exempt` types pay nothing.
fee_rows <- function(data = new25, cap = Inf, body = "len", ext = ext_share, exempt = character(0)) {
  sizes <- lk |>
    mutate(share  = case_when(variant == "ext" ~ ext,
                              variant == "std" ~ 1 - ext,
                              .default = share),
           length = coalesce(.data[[body]], len),
           fee    = if_else(segment %in% exempt, 0, surcharge(length, cap))) |>
    select(make_model, my_from, my_to, segment, verified, share, length, fee)
  inner_join(data, sizes, by = join_by(make_model, between(model_year, my_from, my_to)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")
}
```

## 3. Revenue

Revenue scales the average surcharge among 2025 new registrations up to all `r format(stock, big.mark = ",")` vehicles, assuming the fleet's length mix matches the 2025 registrants'.

**Commercial vehicles.** The DMV file doesn't say which vehicles carry commercial plates, so the "commercial exempt" rows exempt commercial-type vehicles instead: the types listed in `commercial_types`. By default that is full-size vans (Transit, ProMaster, Express/Savana, E-Series, Sprinter, Metris, NV) and heavy-duty pickups (F-250/350/450, Ram 2500/3500). This exempts some personal vans and misses business-owned F-150s and Silverados. Most heavy trucks and buses are already out of the analysis: the DMV puts them in its "All Others" weight class, which both parts leave out.

```{r len_results}
summarise_fees <- function(r, data = new25) {
  r |> summarise(pct_charged     = 100 * sum(n * share * (fee > 0)) / sum(data$n),
                 fee_if_charged  = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(n * share * (fee > 0)),
                 fee_per_car     = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(data$n),
                 rev_2025_cars_M = sum(n * share * fee) / 1e6,
                 rev_fleet_M     = fee_per_car * stock / 1e6)
}

res <- bind_rows(
  "All vehicles, uncapped"      = summarise_fees(fee_rows()),
  "All vehicles, capped"        = summarise_fees(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap)),
  "Commercial exempt, uncapped" = summarise_fees(fee_rows(exempt = commercial_types)),
  "Commercial exempt, capped"   = summarise_fees(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types)),
  .id = "version")
res |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r payer_median, include = FALSE}
wquantile <- function(x, w, p) {
  o  <- order(x)
  cw <- cumsum(w[o]) / sum(w)          # weighted share of payers at or below each fee
  sapply(p, \(q) x[o][which(cw >= q)[1]])
}

r0 <- fee_rows() |> filter(fee > 0)
payer_pct    <- wquantile(r0$fee, r0$n * r0$share, c(0.50, 0.75, 0.90))
median_payer <- payer_pct[1]   # keeps the existing inline text working
```

About `r round(res$pct_charged[1])`% of vehicles are long enough to pay anything. 
The median payer owes $`r round(payer_pct[1])` a year, the 75th percentile $`r round(payer_pct[2])`,
the 90th percentile $`r round(payer_pct[3])`, and the average payer $`r round(res$fee_if_charged[1])`.
Fleet-wide, the surcharge raises about **$`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[1], 1)` million a year uncapped, or $`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[2], 1)` million with a \$`r fee_cap` cap**. Exempting commercial-type vehicles brings that to \$`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[3], 1)` million uncapped, or \$`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[4], 1)` million capped.

## Who pays

Vehicles charged and revenue by type, scaled to the full fleet. `commercial` marks the types exempted in the "commercial exempt" rows.

```{r len_segments}
by_segment <- function(r) {
  r |> group_by(segment) |>
    summarise(cars_charged = sum(n * share * (fee > 0)) / sum(new25$n) * stock,
              revenue_M    = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(new25$n) * stock / 1e6)
}

left_join(by_segment(fee_rows()),
          by_segment(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap)) |> select(segment, revenue_capped_M = revenue_M),
          by = "segment") |>
  mutate(avg_fee_uncapped = 1e6 * revenue_M / cars_charged,
         commercial       = segment %in% commercial_types) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue_M)) |>
  mutate(across(c(cars_charged, avg_fee_uncapped), round), across(starts_with("revenue"), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Sensitivity

Fleet revenue in $ millions.

```{r len_sensitivity}
run_len <- function(...) {
  r <- fee_rows(...)
  round(sum(r$n * r$share * r$fee) / sum(new25$n) * stock / 1e6, 2)
}

variants <- list("Central"                         = list(),
                 "Pickups and vans: shortest body" = list(body = "len_short"),
                 "Pickups and vans: longest body"  = list(body = "len_long"),
                 "No extended-length SUVs"         = list(ext = 0),
                 "Two-thirds extended-length SUVs" = list(ext = 2/3))

imap(variants, \(args, name) tibble(
  variant                    = name,
  uncapped_M                 = do.call(run_len, args),
  capped_M                   = do.call(run_len, c(args, cap = fee_cap)),
  uncapped_comm_exempt_M     = do.call(run_len, c(args, list(exempt = commercial_types))),
  capped_comm_exempt_M       = do.call(run_len, c(args, list(cap = fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types))))) |>
  list_rbind()
```

## Is 2025 a typical year?

Average surcharge per newly registered vehicle by registration year. Earlier files abbreviate more model names, so a few long vehicles go unmatched and older years read slightly low.

```{r len_by_year}
map(2019:2025, \(yr) {
  d <- filter(dmv, year == yr)
  tibble(year     = yr,
         uncapped = sum(with(fee_rows(d), n * share * fee)) / sum(d$n),
         capped   = sum(with(fee_rows(d, cap = fee_cap), n * share * fee)) / sum(d$n))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(c(uncapped, capped), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Caveats

* The estimate is static: it ignores any shift toward shorter vehicles.
* "Commercial" is a proxy based on vehicle type, not registration type (see section 7).
* Scaling 2025 registrations up to the fleet assumes the fleet's length mix matches recent registrants'. The table above suggests that mix has been stable since 2019.

# Checks

```{r checks}
# 1. The lognormal formula matches a simulation
set.seed(1)
mu  <- c(30000, 50000, 90000)
sim <- sapply(mu, \(m) mean(pmax(rlnorm(1e6, log(m) - spread^2 / 2, spread) - threshold, 0)))
round(rbind(formula = expected_excess(mu), simulation = sim))

# 2. Honda and BMW motorcycles are valued as if they were cars in Part 1
bikes <- str_detect(coalesce(dmv$make_model, ""),
  "^BMW (R ?[0-9]|R NINE|K ?[0-9]|F ?[0-9]|S ?1000|C ?[0-9]|CE ?0|G ?[0-9]|M 1000)|^HONDA (CB|CMX|CRF|CTX|GL1|GROM|NC7|NC750|NCH|NCW|NPS|NVA|PCX|VT|XR|Z125|ADV|C125|CH|CN|CT125|WW|XL7)")
c(bikes_still_registered = round(sum(dmv$still_here[bikes])),
  tax_M = round(sum(dmv$still_here[bikes] * dmv$tax[bikes]) / 1e6, 2),
  pct_of_revenue = round(100 * sum(dmv$still_here[bikes] * dmv$tax[bikes]) / sum(dmv$still_here * dmv$tax), 1))

# 3. Share of the 2025 length revenue that rests on lengths checked against
#    manufacturer, dealer or KBB spec pages ("web") vs. the autoevolution dataset or approximations
r <- fee_rows()
r |> group_by(verified) |>
  summarise(pct_of_uncapped_revenue = round(100 * sum(n * share * fee) / sum(r$n * r$share * r$fee), 1))
```

# Sources

* Prices: [KBB average transaction prices, October 2026](https://www.coxautoinc.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/October-2026-Kelley-Blue-Book-Average-Transaction-Price-tables.pdf); [KBB depreciation rates](https://www.kbb.com/car-depreciation).
* Anchor lengths: [2025 Camry, 193.5 in. (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/camry/2025/specs); [2025 Escalade ESV, 227 in. (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/cadillac/escalade-esv/2025/specs).
* Main pickups and vans: [Ford F-150 spec sheet](https://media.ford.com/content/dam/fordmedia/North%20America/US/product/2024/f150/2024%20Ford%20F-150%20Tech%20Specs.pdf); [Ford Transit spec sheet](https://www.fromtheroad.ford.com/content/dam/fordmediasite/us/en/library/2025/specs/2025%20Ford%20Transit%20Technical%20Specifications.pdf); [Chevrolet Express](https://chevrolet.com/commercial/express/vans); [Ram ProMaster (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/ram/promaster/2020/specs/); [Silverado (GM Authority)](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2026/10/2027-chevy-silverado-1500-vs-2026-silverado-1500-exterior-dimensions-compared/); [Ram 1500](https://www.glendaledodgecalifornia.com/research-ram-1500-cabs-boxes.html); [Tundra](https://pickuptrucktalk.com/2021/10/is-the-2022-toyota-tundra-smaller-a-spec-by-spec-comparison/); [Sprinter](https://www.mercedesbenzofwarwick.com/2024-mercedes-benz-sprinter-dimensions/); [E-Series](https://vandimensions.com/database/ford/e-series-2008).
* Large SUVs and minivans: [Tahoe and Suburban](https://www.automotive-fleet.com/news/chevrolet-refreshes-2021-tahoe-and-suburban-suvs); [Escalade generations (GM Authority)](https://gmauthority.com/blog/gm/cadillac/escalade/escalade-esv/); [Yukon](https://www.truedelta.com/GMC-Yukon/specs-103-2021); [Expedition spec sheet](https://www.fromtheroad.ford.com/content/dam/fordmediasite/us/en/library/2025/specs/2025-Ford-Expedition-Technical-Specs.pdf); [minivans (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/compare-cars/results/van-minivan).
* Other lengths: the [autoevolution specs dataset](https://github.com/ilyasozkurt/automobile-models-and-specs) where it has the U.S. model; the rest are marked "approx" in the CSV.
